question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A fine Newfoundland dog was once walking peaceably along a street, when he was assailed by a number of half-starved, worthless curs, who barked at and severely bitten him. The Newfoundland dog, though he might easily have crused them a sharp punishment, only inflicted a slight one, and then quietly proceeded on his way. question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A fine Newfoundland dog, which was passing along a street, in London, splashed with mud, from a carriage, came to a place where some hard dry chips were lying, on which he stepping, shook himself, and thereby shook off a great deal more mud. In the mean time, a little snarling cur, who had all the while been following the large generous creature, with an implacable spirit, came up, and, affecting, also, to shake himself, picked up all the dirt, that remained.

question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A fine Newfoundland dog was once leaping and sporting on the margin of the Shannon, in Ireland. The animal was observed to suddenly arrest his play, and fix his eye and attention on a particular part of the river. He continued to gaze stedfastly for some time, and then plunged in, and rapidly crossed the stream. He landed on the opposite bank, and disappeared. A few minutes he returned, carefully holding in his mouth the ear of a drownning man, which he had just snatched from the wave. question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: An oldNewfoundland dog, who was in the habit of daily watching the departure of the mail-coach from acertain inn in a market-town, had formed an intimate acquaintance with one of the outside passengers, who, on each journey to London, was constantly supplied by his canine friend with a choice rib of beef, which was gratefully received, and punctually restored on the arrival of the coach at the same place on the following evening. question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: When riding through the village of Tarbolton, in Ayrshire, I observed a fine Newfoundland dog. He was marching and jumping at the head of a little procession. A pig was the principal performer. The pig was tied by the leg, and the dog was pulling him to the slaughter-house. I thought, with myself, of the old adage, “It’s an ill wind that blows nobody good.”

question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A fine Newfoundland dog which lived near me, used to leap over the low wall of a neighbouring garden every morning, and go for an airing on the green before the houses. One day he carried some small pieces of wood in his mouth, and after a short time, came back with a large stick in the same manner. He repeated this so many mornings, that the family took notice of it, and saw him plainly gather up several sticks, which they concluded he meant to lay aside against winter. question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A fine old dog, which had long been a faithful companion of my walks, was taken ill, and, after a few days, died. I could not prevail upon myself, to have the poor creature buried in the usual manner, but ordered it to be deeply dug in at the bottom of my garden. I have directed the place to be kept green, and a neat stone to be put over it, with only this inscription, “My poor old friend.”

question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A Newfoundland dog which belonged to a friend of mine, used to go every morning to a certain bakehouse, and buy a penny roll for his break fast. He would carry the penny in his mouth to the shop, and, dropping it down, the baker would take it, and give him the roll, which he would then carry to his kennel. question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A fine Newfoundland dog was once walking quietly along a street in London, when he came to a part where a number of boys were amusing themselves by teasing and barking at an unfortunate littleg, who was almost dead with fright. The large and powerful animal passed on, apparently without bestowing a thought upon the subject, till he arrived at some distance, when, suddenly, turning back, he seized one of the young tormentors by the collar, and, shaking him heartily, passed on, and left him to reflect on his ill-nature.

question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A fine Newfoundland dog was standing on a wharf, waiting for his master, who had gone on board a ship. The gangway was removed, and the ship began to move from the wharf. The dog leaped gallantly into the air, and alighted on the ship. As a reward for his fidelity, his master ordered the vessel to put back, and the grateful animal sprang again upon the wharf.

question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: An amusing instance of canine sagacity was told me the other day. A gentleman was walking in the streets of London, when he observed a little dog, which was a perfect stranger to him, running after him, at some distance, in a very importunate manner. The gentleman, at first, supposed the animal had lost its master, and, as he was moving in the same direction, he naturally concluded it would soon join company with him. question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A fine Newfoundland dog, belonging to a gentleman in Lincolnshire, was greatly attached to a little grandchild, who used to ride on his back. The child dying, the dog was observed to be melancholy, and pined, till he became little better than a skeleton. After some months, he one day disappeared, and was given up for lost. He, however, returned in a few weeks, accompanied by a fine young dog, which he introduced to his master and remaining friends, wagging his stump of a tail, as if desirous of recommending his companion to their notice. question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A Newfoundiand dog, who was a great favorite with everybody, used to accompany his master to church. During the service, he behaved with perfect propriety, and never attempted to quit his place. But no sooner was the benediction pronounced, than he slipped out, and, running to the pond, enjoyed his much-loved sport of bathing. On one occasion, however, he remained so long under water, that some degree of anxiety was expressed lest he should have been seized with cramp. He soon set all fears at rest, by reappearing, and shaking himself, and then gravely walked home.

question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A fine Newfoundland dog was once observed dil gently carrying a basket, which contained a bone, to and fro, between the water-side and his master's house. In the basket, which was his usual burden, he had, unknown to his owner, conveyed a bone to the river; and, after repeated dippings, had brought it dry to land. He then returned for a second ; and, in the course of an hour or two, had thus procured a small heap of bones. question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A fine Newfoundland dog was standing on a bridge, watching some boys who were bathing in the river. The boys teased and provoked him, and at last one of them. dived into the water, and, coming unexpectedly behind the dog, seized him by the tail. The intelligent animal did not, at first, attempt to retaliate, but, as soon as he had shaken off hisacious assailant, he deliberately walked into the water, and, seizing the boy by the collar, held him quietly and firmly, until a person, who had been a silent spectator of the whole scene

question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A fine Newfoundland dog, which was great favourite of mine, used to accompany me homewards, whenever I went a great distance into the city. question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: One day last week, as I was passing along Cheapside, I observed a fine specimen of the equestrian art, in the shape of a beautiful black horse, which pranced and curvetted in a manner that drew the eyes of all the bystanders. Upon making some inquiries, I found he was the private property of a gentleman, a member of the Royal College of Surgeons, who had purchased him for the sum of sixty guineas, merely on account of his extraordinary sagacity and docility. question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A fine Newfoundland dog, which was greatly attached to his master, used to watch over him when he was asleep. One night the gentleman, on going to bed, directed his favorite to be shut out of the room, as he had some particular papers to examine. The dog, however, remained under the window. The gentleman, after some hours, went to bed, and the animal was again ordered to be turned out, but still he refused to leave the spot. question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A fine Newfoundland dog was once walking along a street, in a lonely part of the town, at night. A thief saw him, and thought to rob and murder him. He accordingly followed him, at a distance, till he saw him stop before a house. Then he came up, and setzed him by the throat. The dog struggled, and barked. question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A fine Newfoundland dog, which was daily in the habit of crossing the river Thames, from Westminster to Lambeth, had, on a particular occasion, been taken to Greenwich, by water. On the following morning, the animal, instead of going to the accustomed place in Westminster, from whence he had been used to set out, went down to the Green-hithe, in the Borough, and, after some little delay, quietly and deliberately walked into a boat, and presented himself on board a Gravesend vessel, which had come up the preceding evening, but which he had never before visited. question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A fine Newfoundland dog was once walking peaceably along a street in London, when he was attacked by a hungry mastiff much larger than himself. The Newfoundland dog, being too proud to bark at a

question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A fine Newfoundland dog was recently the means of preserving a child from drowning, at Norwich. The animal sprang into the water, and, seizing the boy by the clothes, swam with him to the shore. The boy had fallen through the ice.

question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: I was once riding through a beautiful country, and came to a river, which I wished to cross, but there was no bridge. I therefore determined to ford it. The stream was swift, but the bottom appeared firm and smooth. I proceeded, in, and had nearly reached the opposite side in safety, when suddenly my horse's foot slipped, and in an instant he was borne down the current. question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A Newfoundland dog, which was a great favourite with everybody in the neighbourhood in which he lived, used to go every day and fetch the baker’s, loaf. He would carry the bread in his mouth to a poor sick woman, who gratefully received it. One morning the dog came without the loaf, and, going to the woman, laid the penny, which he had stolen, at her feet.

question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: An eminent French savant was inordinately fond of horses, and was accustomed to pass a portion of every summer in the country. One day, in the course of a ride, he came to a bridge, which he was about to cross, when his horse suddenly stopped. All the whipping and spurring in the world would not stir him a step further. question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A fine Newfoundland dog, belonging to a gentleman in the neighborhood of London, displayed great sagacity in saving the life of a child. The child, being left alone in a room, approached too near the fire, and had its dress set in a blaze. The cries of the little sufferer attracted the attention of the dog, who seized the burning garment in his teeth, and, notwithstanding the smart he must have experienced, carried the child safely out of doors.

question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: One day last week, as I was walking along Cheapside, I observed a fine Newfound land dog standing at the corner of a street, keeping watch over a basket full of. The owner of the dog had gone into a shop, and left his faithful guardian in charge of the property; and so long as I continued in sight, the dog never suffered a single orange to be touched by any passenger, by whom his civilities were several times re.

question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A fine Newfoundland dog, belonging to a gentleman in London, leaped into the Thames, and saved from drowning a little boy, who had fallen overboard. The owner of the dog was so pleased with the animal's sagacity and humanity, that he had a collar made, with the following inscription:-"Honest, brave, and faithful." The dog lived several years afterward, and fully justified his master in the opinion he had formed of him.

question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A fine Newfoundland dog was once observed to stop in the midst of his career, to rescue from drowning a little pet spaniel, which had fallen into the water. He seized him by the collar, and, with great difficulty, dragged him to land. The little spaniel was quite unconscious, but the generous Newfoundland, shook himself, and, hanging his wet coat on the pales, lickd the spaniel dry. The writer of this anecdote had it from the observation of an eye witness.

question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A fine St. Bernard dog, which was presented to me when quite a young pup, used to follow me to school every morning, and, remaining quiet so long as I was there, would return home with me in the afternoon. But one day, I having chastised him for some offence, he resentfully hid himself, and, a few days after, followed me as usual to the school-house door. question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A fine old horse, which had long carried a. general in the army, was turned out to spend the remainder of his days in a pleasant pasture. Here, however, he was not destined to remain long in quiet; for, after some time, he was claimed by a younger son, who wanted to finish his education at the university. The poor horse was, therefore, obliged, once more, to change his place of residence, and was carried to Oxford. But, who can describe the feelings of the poor animal, on being a second time sequestered from all his former acquaintance.

question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A fine Newfoundland dog, which was passing through a street, stopped to gaze at some pups at play. The puppies, accustomed only to human playmates, ran towards the stranger with great signs of friendship. The large dog, however, gently repressed their advances, and, at last, with a kind of sorrowful wag of the tail, walked on. The different natures of the two species were clearly shown. question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A Newfoundlander, who was very fond of dogs, used to walk daily on a particular street. On a certain day he observed a dog, whom he had long known and regarded with great affection, at the point of death. He hired a cab, and had the dying creature carried home to his own house, where, in a few hours, it breathed its last in his arms.

question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A fine Newfoundland dog, which was greatly attached to its master, a sailor, used to watch hour after hour for his return at night. The poor animal would bark to announce his coming, and leap upon him with every mark of delight when he appeared. But, on one occasion, his joy was turned into grief; for the sailor fell from his plank, and was drowned. question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: An old Newfoundlander, who lived in a seaport town, had a fine, large, black dog, of which he was very fond. question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A fine St. Bernard dog was standing on a bridge, waiting for his master, who had gone on before. A little child, wandering about, fell into the river. The dog, instantly comprehending the situation, plunged in, and seizing the child by its clothes, bore it safely to the shore. The delighted parent took up the tiny burden, and pressed it to his bosom. The dog, standing meekly by, looked up in his face, wagging his tail, as if to ask, "Well, didn't I do it well?"

question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A fine Newfoundland dog was once walking along a street in London, when he came to a part where a number of boys were bowling and fighting. The noble animal paused a moment to contemplate the disgraceful scene. At length, unable to endure it longer, he walked up to the combatants, and, seizing the first boy he could lay hold of by the collar, thrust him into the midst of the road, and, returning, did the same to a second and a third. question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A fine Newfoundland dog, which was daily accustomed to plunge into the sea, from the beach at Brighton, to bring ashore the bathers who had ventured too far, at length became disabled by the loss of one of his claws. But, incredible as it may appear, the intelligent creature continued to perform his wonted service, after his mutilation; and, having lost one of his rowing feet, actually pulled a gallant oar with the other, to perfect safety, every day, for a fortnight.

question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.

question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A fine Newfoundland dog, which was passing along Fleet Street, stopped to drink at a shop where some beer was spilt in the gutter. A number of small ill-natured snarling curs, in the meantime, barked at him from the adjoining pavement. "Go thy ways, poor fools," said the generous, good-natured Newfoundlander, "and learn to pity, rather than insult, the misfortunes of the miserable."

question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A fine Newfoundland dog, which was passing along a street, happened to spy a littleant, which had fallen into the water. He plunged in, seized him by the neck, and, with great difficulty, brought him safe to land. The spectators, who had assembled on the occasion, rewarded the noble animal with a plentiful shower of blows, for detaining them in the street, and, when he retired, expressed their indignation at his inhumanity, in thus ill-treating an animal so much smaller than himself. question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A fine Newfoundland dog was standing on the shore, watching very attentively a ship which had just come into the port. The moment any of the crew appeared upon deck, the animal evinced great signs of pleasure; but when a poor little apprentice boy came alone upon the rigging, the dog leaped into the sea, and, swimming around the vessel, continued his caresses to the lad, until he was taken in.

question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.

question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: I was riding through Hyde Park, and saw a beautiful blackg, that was gamboling about, in the fulness of health and ildren. I thought of the many hours of lonely pleasure that uimal must have had, in its quiet rambles, and envied it be happiness of them.

question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A fine Newfoundland dog, which was passing along a street in the city, happened to spy some meat in a butcher's shop, which had been laid down, for a minute, upon the flags. In an instant, he darted into the shop, seized the coveted dainty in his mouth, and, as quickly, darting out again, scampered away, with it, down the nearest avenue. question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A fine Newfoundland dog was once leaping and playing about a ship of war. The animal was great favorite, and had come to be regarded, in some sort, as one of the crew. The sailors had taught him a variety of clever tricks, and Black, or, as he was called, "Our Black, !" was the pet and amusement of all hands. One day "Black" was missing. question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: I was once riding through a country town, and stopped to admire a fine horse, which was grazing in a field by the roadside. The owner of the animal came out of the house, and I asked him if that was a good horse to go in harness. "Oh, yes," said he, "he is a good horse, and a kind one, too, for he never kicked, or bited, or did anything bad, in his life." question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A fine Newfoundland dog was once walking peaceably along a street, when he was attacked by a number of little curs, who barked furiously at him. The great dog, disdaining to notice the small fry, went quietly on his way. But, in the same street, he was assailed by a mastiff; and now, thought he, I must show what I can do. So he turned round, and, in less time than I take to tell it, sent his antagonist howling into the gutter. Proceed, Sir.

question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A fine St. Bernard dog was standing on a bridge, waiting for the arrival of a train. The dog knew that it brought his master, and, in due time, the train came up. The passengers got out, and, among them, a little child, which had somehow lost hold of its mothers hand, in the confusion of a long journey. question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A fine Newfoundland dog, which was passing along a street in London, sprang forward to rescue from drowning a little child, who had fallen into a tank of water. The heroic animal succeeded in bringing the child safe to land, but, in so doing, he, himself, unfortunately, received injuries, from which he died.

question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A fine Newfoundland dog was once leaping and playing on the banks of the Thames. He saw in the water a poor little lap-dog, that had fallen from a steamboat. The poor little creature was drowning; and, what could not swim, of course, could not help itself. The brave, generous, great dog, plunged in, brought the little one to land, and laid it safely at the feet of its grateful mistress.

question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: When driving through Wales, I was always pleased to see the respect which the people had for a fine horse. If I stopped at a little alehouse to get a draught of cider, and a feed of oats for my horse, the ostler would come out and hold the animal’s head, while I refreshed myself within. One evening, just as the shades of night were falling, I drew up at such a place, and, alighting, desired the man to attend to my horse. question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A fine Newfoundland dog, belonging to a gentleman in the North of Scotland, was recently the means of saving a little boy from drowning. The child, in crossing a small river, fell into the water, and, but for the gallant conduct of the dog, must have perished. The sagacious animal, who happened to be standing near, plunged into the stream, and, catching the boy by the clothes, with great difficulty drew him to the bank. question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A few days ago, I saw a fine Newfoundland dog watching patiently for some time, beside a green grocer's basket, which contained meat, pies, and other articles, too tempting to be resisted by idle dogs. At last, a poor, hungry-looking cur, came sneaking past, who no sooner caught sight of the basket, than, quick as thought, away went he, with it, at full gallop. question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A fine Newfoundland dog belonging to a gentleman in the North of Scotland, spring a few days ago into the sea, and rescued from drowning a little boy, the son of one of the fishermen. The child had ventured too far, and, getting beyond his depth, was in great danger. The dog, who happened at the time to be playing on the beach, saw his predicament, and, instantly plunging into the waves, brought him safe to land. question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A few days ago, as I was walking along Cheapside, I observed a fine, large dog, of the Newfoundland species, calmly contemplating himself in a looking-glass, which was suspended at the shop of a bird-fancier. The pleased expression of the animal’s countenance satisfied me that he was perfectly well aware of the great improvement which the late brilliant polish had made in his personal appearance. So, thinking of the vast number of vain human beings, who waste so much time in a similar way, I resolved to record the fact in my Diary.

question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A fine St. Bernard dog, named Barry, was once the means of saving a child from being run over in a London street. Barry was walking quietly along, when he heard the cries of a little boy. He at once stopped, and, looking round, saw a small child in great peril, for a horse was close upon him. The intelligent Barry sprang forward, caught up the boy in his mouth, and bore him out of harm's way to a place of safety. The child, when questioned, said he was only "playing at horses." Barry died soon after this good deed

question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A fine Newfoundland dog, which was lately the companion of my walks, used to exhibit symptoms of pleasure whenever he passed a shop where he had been treated to a penny loaf. On the last day of his life, he crawled, as he was accustomed to do, to his place of feeding; but, alas! he crawled there to die. After licking the hand which used to caress him, he licked his fatal present, and, immediately falling into convulsions, expired.

question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: A fine Newfoundland dog, which was greatly attached to its master, a surgeon in extensive practice, accompanied him in all his rounds, to the great terror of timid patients. The dog, at last, became ill, and could no longer leave the house. On the recovery of the dog, the master removed to another part of the town, still more distant from the fields. The animal, however, was not to be baffled, and, after some weeks, re-appeared, having, by some means, again traced out his former haunts.

question: Relate a brief anecdote about an animal you admire.
answer: I was riding along a country lane the other day, and saw a fine St. Bernard dog, standing by the side of the road, and looking the picture of intelligent animation.
